data.name: Hirunika
data.gender_notes: Hirunika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hirunika is derived from the Sanskrit words 'hira' meaning 'sky' and 'nikā' meaning 'jewel'. This name signifies the beauty of the night sky, often associated with the divine and the celestial. The name Hirunika carries the meaning “Sky-Jewel” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hirunika usually hope their child will grow to embody sky-jewel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by the divine, carrying the energy of the heavens and the depth of the cosmos.
data.etymology: Hirunika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sky-Jewel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hirunika total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_sanskrit.name: हिरुणिका
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Hirunika is derived from the Sanskrit word हिरू (Hiru), which means 'head' and निका (Nikā), which means 'Goddess'. The name Hirunika signifies the Goddess who resides on the head. In Hindu mythology, the Goddess Shringini, also known as Shringamata or Shringaraparvathi, is the Goddess of the head and is often depicted as the consort of Lord Shiva. The name Hirunika may be used as a tribute to this revered deity.

Named after the sky (hira) and the precious jewel (nikā), Hirunika represents the captivating beauty of the night with its starry sky dotted with bright jewels, inspiring awe and reverence.

historical_references.reference: Hirunika was a legendary queen of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling in the late 2nd or early 1st century BCE. She is best known for her contributions to the construction of the Prakasasila Dam and the Agastya Theertham tank in Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh.
historical_references.context: Legendary queen of the Satavahana dynasty

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Hirunika is found in the Mahabharata, where she is mentioned as the sister of Bhima, one of the Pandava brothers. No specific time period is mentioned in this reference.
